title: Choosing -nsa or -nsä
summary: The third-person ending has two vowel-harmony forms, -nsa and -nsä. Choose it from the noun’s vowels, not from hänen or heidän.
objectives: Choose -nsa or -nsä from the noun’s vowels, including neutral e and i.
Recognise the pattern, then produce it with the supporting words shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: The third-person ending has two vowel-harmony forms, -nsa and -nsä. Choose it from the noun’s vowels, not from hänen or heidän.

If the noun has a, o, or u, choose -nsa: pallonsa, kirjansa, autonsa. With ä, ö, y and no back vowel, choose -nsä: kynänsä, tyynynsä. Neutral e and i allow a back vowel elsewhere to decide; with only neutral vowels the front ending is used.
This lesson uses regular singular naming forms. Other noun cases may use other third-person ending patterns; those are taught later.
keyPoints: Practise one singular possessed thing with the supporting forms shown.

steps: Hänen names a single owner; choose the suffix vowels from the noun.
Pallo (“ball”) contains back vowels a/o: pallo + -nsa = pallonsa. The ä in hänen does not choose the suffix.
Use the same single-owner pronoun hänen.
Kynä (“pen”) has front vowels y/ä and no back vowel: kynä + -nsä = kynänsä.
Heidän means “their”; it does not choose the suffix vowels.
Kirja (“book”) has back vowel a despite neutral i: kirja + -nsa = kirjansa.
Peli (“game”) has only neutral vowels e/i, so choose the front ending: peli + -nsä = pelinsä.

commonMistakes: Choose -nsa or -nsä from the noun, not from the vowels in hänen or heidän.
A back vowel takes -nsa even with neutral e/i: kirja → kirjansa.
A front-vowel or neutral-only noun takes -nsä in this inventory: kynä → kynänsä and peli → pelinsä.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Choose the final vowel in “their pen”: heidän kynäns_. Use kynä (“pen”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Use ä: kynä becomes kynänsä. With no back vowel, front vowels or only neutral e and i require -nsä. Choose from the noun, not the owner pronoun.
practiceExercises.misconceptionCategory: Third-person possessive vowel harmony: form or meaning confused

optionFeedback.a: Use a only when the noun contains a back vowel a, o, or u.
optionFeedback.ä: Use ä: kynä becomes kynänsä. With no back vowel, front vowels or only neutral e and i require -nsä. Choose from the noun, not the owner pronoun.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Write the final vowel in “his pillow”: hänen tyynyns_. Use tyyny (“pillow”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Use ä: tyyny becomes tyynynsä. With no back vowel, front vowels or only neutral e and i require -nsä. Choose from the noun, not the owner pronoun.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Choose the final vowel in “his car”: hänen autons_. Use auto (“car”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Use a: auto becomes autonsa. A back vowel a, o, or u requires -nsa. Choose from the noun, not the owner pronoun.

optionFeedback.a: Use a: auto becomes autonsa. A back vowel a, o, or u requires -nsa. Choose from the noun, not the owner pronoun.
optionFeedback.ä: Use ä when there is no back vowel: front vowels or only neutral e and i take -nsä.
